newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia says East Timor not behind U.N. defeat.
newsitem.headline: Australia says East Timor not behind U.N. defeat.

text.p: Australia said on Thursday there was no evidence that the issue of the former Portuguese colony of East Timor had affected a vote for a U.N. Security Council seat which Canberra lost to Lisbon.
Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said he was surprised after Canberra lost Monday's vote for a non-permanent Security Council seat to Portugal, 124 votes to 57.

Australia is one of a handful of Western countries that recognises Indonesia's rule in East Timor after Jakarta invaded the territory in December 1975 and declared the enclave its 27th province the following year.
The United Nations still recognises Portugal as being the administering power.
Downer, in Jakarta for an Australia-Indonesian Ministerial Forum, was asked at a news conference whether the issue of East Timor had any bearing on the United Nations vote.
"I see no evidence that (East Timor) has had any bearing on the outcome of the vote. What had a bearing on the outcome of the vote we don't know," he said.
"Our mission in New York is spending a fair bit of time to assess what happened. It's not easy to do as it is a secret ballot," Downer said.
The Australian newspaper on Thursday quoted senior U.N. and United States officials in New York as saying France had played a key role in thwarting Australia's bid.
Its backing of Portugal was seen as retaliation for last year's bitter row with Australia over nuclear testing in the South Pacific.
Earlier this month, East Timorese bishop Carlos Belo and a resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta were jointly awarded the Nobel peace prize, putting the spotlight back on East Timor.
